detail.overview:
Introduction - Everest Base Camp Trek - 14 Days

The Everest Base Camp Trek is one of Nepal's most rewarding journeys, taking you through Kathmandu, Lukla, Phakding and beyond. This 14-day journey is guided by experienced local leaders and combines landscapes, culture and comfortable, well-paced days.

The journey combines scenery, local culture and carefully planned rest days. The highlight is reaching Everest Base Camp (5,364 m), with time to take in the views, meet local people and enjoy the journey at your own pace.

Everest Base Camp Trek – 14 Days at a Glance

  • Duration: 14 days
  • Destination: Nepal
  • Maximum altitude: 5,364 m
  • Starting and ending point: Kathmandu
  • Difficulty: Moderate
  • Accommodation: Hotel and teahouse
  • Group size: 1–12
  • Best seasons: Autumn and Spring

Why choose our 14-day Everest Base Camp Trek?

  • Experienced, government-licensed local guides
  • Small groups of up to 12 travelers
  • Carefully planned itinerary with rest days
  • All required permits arranged
  • Guaranteed departures and private departures available
  • Responsible tourism that supports local communities

Highlights of Everest Base Camp Trek – 14 Days

  • Reach Everest Base Camp at 5,364 m
  • Pass through Lukla, Phakding, Namche Bazaar with a local guide
  • Experience authentic local culture and traditions
  • Enjoy breathtaking mountain and valley scenery
  • Stay in comfortable hotels and welcoming local lodges

Everest Base Camp Trek: Elevation and Stops

  • Starting Point: Kathmandu: 1,350 m
  • Lukla: 2,860 m
  • Phakding: 2,610 m
  • Namche Bazaar: 3,440 m
  • Tengboche: 3,867 m
  • Dingboche: 4,410 m

  • Everest Base Camp: 5,364 m

detail.packingListIntro:
One of the hardest things is packing for a trek in Nepal's Himalayas. You have to know what to take with you on the trip and what to leave behind. Under- or overpacking is a dreadful idea.

We assign a porter for every 2 trekkers. Each porter carries about 20 kilograms (10 kg per person), and domestic flights have their own weight limit, so pack light and keep your main luggage to about 10 kg.

Basic Essential

  • Trekking boots: carry sturdy, well broken-in boots.
  • Daypack (30-45L) with rain cover: for your daily necessities.
  • Duffle bag (60-70L): carried by a porter, keep it to about 10 kg.
  • Sleeping bag: one rated at least -15 is advised in winter.

Trekking Equipment

  • Trekking poles
  • Gaiters for the rainy and winter season
  • Torchlight or headlamp with spare batteries
  • Refillable water bottle

Clothing

Upper part of the body (head, face and neck)

  • Sunglasses
  • Scarf or face mask
  • Sunscreen (SPF 50+)
  • Sun hat or cap
  • Woolen hat

Middle part of the body (chest, stomach and hands)

  • Trekking shirts
  • Thermal wear
  • Fleece jacket
  • Gloves
  • Windproof jacket
  • Raincoat and rain trousers
  • Down jacket

Lower part of the body (thighs, legs and feet)

  • Trekking trousers (quick-dry, water-resistant)
  • Fleece trousers or woolen pants
  • Socks and undergarments
  • Sandals or crocs

Other optional items

  • Spare batteries for the camera
  • Playing cards and reading books

Documents

  • A passport with a few copies
  • 2 passport-size photos
  • Money for the trip (US dollars or euros)
  • Personal medicine and a doctor's prescription, if needed
  • Travel insurance
  • Emergency contact details

We provide: duffel bags, sleeping bags and down jackets upon request. This gear is to be returned to us after you finish your trek.

Tips: if you do not have the items listed above, you can also buy them in Kathmandu.

detail.packingListIntro:
One of the hardest things is packing for a trek in Nepal's Himalayas. You have to know what to take with you on the trip and what to leave behind. Under- or overpacking is a dreadful idea.

We assign a porter for every 2 trekkers. Each porter carries about 20 kilograms (10 kg per person), and domestic flights have their own weight limit, so pack light and keep your main luggage to about 10 kg.

Basic Essential

  • Trekking boots: carry sturdy, well broken-in boots.
  • Daypack (30-45L) with rain cover: for your daily necessities.
  • Duffle bag (60-70L): carried by a porter, keep it to about 10 kg.
  • Sleeping bag: one rated at least -15 is advised in winter.

Trekking Equipment

  • Trekking poles
  • Gaiters for the rainy and winter season
  • Torchlight or headlamp with spare batteries
  • Refillable water bottle

Clothing

Upper part of the body (head, face and neck)

  • Sunglasses
  • Scarf or face mask
  • Sunscreen (SPF 50+)
  • Sun hat or cap
  • Woolen hat

Middle part of the body (chest, stomach and hands)

  • Trekking shirts
  • Thermal wear
  • Fleece jacket
  • Gloves
  • Windproof jacket
  • Raincoat and rain trousers
  • Down jacket

Lower part of the body (thighs, legs and feet)

  • Trekking trousers (quick-dry, water-resistant)
  • Fleece trousers or woolen pants
  • Socks and undergarments
  • Sandals or crocs

Other optional items

  • Spare batteries for the camera
  • Playing cards and reading books

Documents

  • A passport with a few copies
  • 2 passport-size photos
  • Money for the trip (US dollars or euros)
  • Personal medicine and a doctor's prescription, if needed
  • Travel insurance
  • Emergency contact details

We provide: duffel bags, sleeping bags and down jackets upon request. This gear is to be returned to us after you finish your trek.

Tips: if you do not have the items listed above, you can also buy them in Kathmandu.

  • Maximum altitude: 3,860 m
  • Starting and ending point: Kathmandu
  • Difficulty: Moderate
  • Accommodation: Hotel and teahouse
  • Group size: 1–12
  • Best seasons: Autumn and Spring

detail.packingListIntro:
One of the hardest things is packing for a trek in Nepal's Himalayas. You have to know what to take with you on the trip and what to leave behind. Under- or overpacking is a dreadful idea.

We assign a porter for every 2 trekkers. Each porter carries about 20 kilograms (10 kg per person), and domestic flights have their own weight limit, so pack light and keep your main luggage to about 10 kg.

Basic Essential

  • Trekking boots: carry sturdy, well broken-in boots.
  • Daypack (30-45L) with rain cover: for your daily necessities.
  • Duffle bag (60-70L): carried by a porter, keep it to about 10 kg.
  • Sleeping bag: one rated at least -15 is advised in winter.

Trekking Equipment

  • Trekking poles
  • Gaiters for the rainy and winter season
  • Torchlight or headlamp with spare batteries
  • Refillable water bottle

Clothing

Upper part of the body (head, face and neck)

  • Sunglasses
  • Scarf or face mask
  • Sunscreen (SPF 50+)
  • Sun hat or cap
  • Woolen hat

Middle part of the body (chest, stomach and hands)

  • Trekking shirts
  • Thermal wear
  • Fleece jacket
  • Gloves
  • Windproof jacket
  • Raincoat and rain trousers
  • Down jacket

Lower part of the body (thighs, legs and feet)

  • Trekking trousers (quick-dry, water-resistant)
  • Fleece trousers or woolen pants
  • Socks and undergarments
  • Sandals or crocs

Other optional items

  • Spare batteries for the camera
  • Playing cards and reading books

Documents

  • A passport with a few copies
  • 2 passport-size photos
  • Money for the trip (US dollars or euros)
  • Personal medicine and a doctor's prescription, if needed
  • Travel insurance
  • Emergency contact details

We provide: duffel bags, sleeping bags and down jackets upon request. This gear is to be returned to us after you finish your trek.

Tips: if you do not have the items listed above, you can also buy them in Kathmandu.

detail.packingListIntro:
One of the hardest things is packing for a trek in Nepal's Himalayas. You have to know what to take with you on the trip and what to leave behind. Under- or overpacking is a dreadful idea.

We assign a porter for every 2 trekkers. Each porter carries about 20 kilograms (10 kg per person), and domestic flights have their own weight limit, so pack light and keep your main luggage to about 10 kg.

Basic Essential

  • Trekking boots: carry sturdy, well broken-in boots.
  • Daypack (30-45L) with rain cover: for your daily necessities.
  • Duffle bag (60-70L): carried by a porter, keep it to about 10 kg.
  • Sleeping bag: one rated at least -15 is advised in winter.

Trekking Equipment

  • Trekking poles
  • Gaiters for the rainy and winter season
  • Torchlight or headlamp with spare batteries
  • Refillable water bottle

Clothing

Upper part of the body (head, face and neck)

  • Sunglasses
  • Scarf or face mask
  • Sunscreen (SPF 50+)
  • Sun hat or cap
  • Woolen hat

Middle part of the body (chest, stomach and hands)

  • Trekking shirts
  • Thermal wear
  • Fleece jacket
  • Gloves
  • Windproof jacket
  • Raincoat and rain trousers
  • Down jacket

Lower part of the body (thighs, legs and feet)

  • Trekking trousers (quick-dry, water-resistant)
  • Fleece trousers or woolen pants
  • Socks and undergarments
  • Sandals or crocs

Other optional items

  • Spare batteries for the camera
  • Playing cards and reading books

Documents

  • A passport with a few copies
  • 2 passport-size photos
  • Money for the trip (US dollars or euros)
  • Personal medicine and a doctor's prescription, if needed
  • Travel insurance
  • Emergency contact details

We provide: duffel bags, sleeping bags and down jackets upon request. This gear is to be returned to us after you finish your trek.

Tips: if you do not have the items listed above, you can also buy them in Kathmandu.

detail.overview:
Introduction - Nepal Tibet Bhutan Tour - 21 Days

The Nepal Tibet Bhutan Tour is one of Nepal's most rewarding journeys, taking you through Kathmandu, Lhasa, Paro and beyond. This 21-day journey is guided by experienced local leaders and combines landscapes, culture and comfortable, well-paced days.

The journey combines scenery, local culture and carefully planned rest days. The highlight is reaching Punakha (3,650 m), with time to take in the views, meet local people and enjoy the journey at your own pace.

Nepal Tibet Bhutan Tour – 21 Days at a Glance

  • Duration: 21 days
  • Destination: Nepal, Tibet and Bhutan
  • Maximum altitude: 3,650 m
  • Starting and ending point: Kathmandu
  • Difficulty: Easy
  • Accommodation: Hotel and lodge
  • Group size: 1–12
  • Best seasons: March to May and September to November

Why choose our 21-day Nepal Tibet Bhutan Tour?

  • Experienced, government-licensed local guides
  • Small groups of up to 12 travelers
  • Carefully planned itinerary with rest days
  • All required permits arranged
  • Guaranteed departures and private departures available
  • Responsible tourism that supports local communities

Highlights of Nepal Tibet Bhutan Tour – 21 Days

  • Reach Punakha at 3,650 m
  • Pass through Lhasa, Paro, Thimphu with a local guide
  • Experience authentic local culture and traditions
  • Enjoy breathtaking mountain and valley scenery
  • Stay in comfortable hotels and welcoming local lodges

Nepal Tibet Bhutan Tour: Elevation and Stops

  • Starting Point: Kathmandu: 1,350 m
  • Lhasa: 3,650 m
  • Paro: 2,280 m
  • Thimphu: 2,320 m
  • Punakha: 1,250 m

What to Expect on the 21-Day Nepal Tibet Bhutan Tour

Expect an unforgettable journey from Kathmandu to Punakha, with experienced local guides and a well-designed itinerary. Daily distances are manageable, and you will have time to rest, take photographs and meet local people along the way.

Nepal Tibet Bhutan Tour – Route Map & Itinerary

  • You will follow the Kathmandu → Lhasa → Paro → Thimphu → Punakha route on this 21-day trip — find the route map and the daily plan in detail below.

What to Expect on the 1-Day Bhaktapur and Patan Day Tour

Expect an unforgettable journey from Kathmandu to Lumbini, with experienced local guides and a well-designed itinerary. Daily distances are manageable, and you will have time to rest, take photographs and meet local people along the way.

detail.packingListIntro:
One of the hardest things is packing for a trek in Nepal's Himalayas. You have to know what to take with you on the trip and what to leave behind. Under- or overpacking is a dreadful idea.

We assign a porter for every 2 trekkers. Each porter carries about 20 kilograms (10 kg per person), and domestic flights have their own weight limit, so pack light and keep your main luggage to about 10 kg.

Basic Essential

  • Trekking boots: carry sturdy, well broken-in boots.
  • Daypack (30-45L) with rain cover: for your daily necessities.
  • Duffle bag (60-70L): carried by a porter, keep it to about 10 kg.
  • Sleeping bag: one rated at least -15 is advised in winter.

Trekking Equipment

  • Trekking poles
  • Gaiters for the rainy and winter season
  • Torchlight or headlamp with spare batteries
  • Refillable water bottle

Clothing

Upper part of the body (head, face and neck)

  • Sunglasses
  • Scarf or face mask
  • Sunscreen (SPF 50+)
  • Sun hat or cap
  • Woolen hat

Middle part of the body (chest, stomach and hands)

  • Trekking shirts
  • Thermal wear
  • Fleece jacket
  • Gloves
  • Windproof jacket
  • Raincoat and rain trousers
  • Down jacket

Lower part of the body (thighs, legs and feet)

  • Trekking trousers (quick-dry, water-resistant)
  • Fleece trousers or woolen pants
  • Socks and undergarments
  • Sandals or crocs

Other optional items

  • Spare batteries for the camera
  • Playing cards and reading books

Documents

  • A passport with a few copies
  • 2 passport-size photos
  • Money for the trip (US dollars or euros)
  • Personal medicine and a doctor's prescription, if needed
  • Travel insurance
  • Emergency contact details

We provide: duffel bags, sleeping bags and down jackets upon request. This gear is to be returned to us after you finish your trek.

Tips: if you do not have the items listed above, you can also buy them in Kathmandu.

knowBeforeYouGo.heading: Altitude and acclimatization
knowBeforeYouGo.body: Our itineraries include rest days so your body can adjust to the altitude. Walk slowly, drink plenty of water and tell your guide straight away if you feel unwell.

knowBeforeYouGo.heading: Permits and entry
knowBeforeYouGo.body: We arrange all trekking permits. Please bring your passport and two passport-size photos, and arrive in Kathmandu at least one day before the trip starts.

knowBeforeYouGo.heading: Accommodation and food
knowBeforeYouGo.body: You stay in hotels in the city and in simple local teahouses on the trail. Meals are freshly cooked from a menu of local and international dishes.

knowBeforeYouGo.heading: Travel insurance
knowBeforeYouGo.body: Travel insurance that covers emergency evacuation at altitude is required for all trekkers.

questions.question: Can I do the Bhaktapur and Patan Day Tour as a private trip?
questions.answer: Yes. Private departures are available on any date of the year for solo travelers, couples, friends and families — an additional fee applies.

questions.question: Where does the Bhaktapur and Patan Day Tour start?
questions.answer: The trip starts and ends in Kathmandu. The trip date is your arrival date in the city.

questions.question: How many hours do we travel or walk each day?
questions.answer: Expect about 2-4 hours on a typical day, with shorter days for arrival, rest and departure.

questions.question: What is included in the 1-day Bhaktapur and Patan Day Tour?
questions.answer: Airport transfers, accommodation, meals as listed, an experienced guide, all permits and the transport in the itinerary are included.

questions.question: What is the best time for the Bhaktapur and Patan Day Tour?
questions.answer: The best seasons are autumn and spring, when skies are clearest and conditions most comfortable.

questions.question: How difficult is the Bhaktapur and Patan Day Tour?
questions.answer: The trip is rated easy. No technical experience is needed, but a reasonable level of fitness helps.

questions.question: Can beginners do the Bhaktapur and Patan Day Tour?
questions.answer: Yes. With some preparation and a steady pace, most healthy travelers complete it comfortably.

questions.question: How fit do I need to be?
questions.answer: Regular walking, cycling or swimming for a few weeks beforehand is enough for most travelers.

questions.question: What food is available during the trip?
questions.answer: Freshly cooked breakfast, lunch and dinner with local and international dishes; vegetarian meals are always available.

questions.question: What type of accommodation is available?
questions.answer: Hotel and lodge — twin-share rooms, with single rooms available for an additional fee.
